summary: Clear Creek County, CO: a temporary Forest Service lookout building on the Mount Evans summit, built 1942; it stood only a couple of years; the summit is a public trail destination.

facts.design: Temporary lookout building at the summit
facts.status_note: OuterSpatial says the lookout remained only a couple of years

access.note: Summit trail is never closed to use; the road to the trailhead is closed to motorized use from Labor Day until Memorial Day

visit.trail_note: Trail to the summit starts at a parking area; the trail was improved in 1945 after the road reopened

events.note: Built for the US Forest Service as a temporary lookout building; a photo captioned 8/14/42 shows it

notes_for_editor: Two sources. The register gives the 1942 build, the temporary building, the purpose caption and the elevation, but has no removal field. The 'gone' status and 'couple of years' rest on OuterSpatial alone, and no removal date was found, so the story gives none. No source describes what remains at the 1942 site. The Crest House (a restaurant built 1941, burned 1979, walls remain) is a different structure and is named in the story only to avoid confusion. The FFLA Colorado page (ffla.org/cohost-co/evans.html) returned 404. The brief's kind 'ground' fits a building; no tower is described. Access is from OuterSpatial and the summit road status may change seasonally, so the story says so.
